title: esbuild refuses top-level await under the cjs output format
claim: esbuild fails the whole bundle when an entrypoint uses top-level await and the output format is cjs, so a script that runs correctly under tsx cannot be bundled without being wrapped in a function.
appliesTo: Environment not reported by the submitter.
expectation: a script that runs under tsx bundles for the same runtime, since both target the same Node version
reality: the build fails with 'Top-level await is currently not supported with the cjs output format', naming the await line, and the script ships unbundled or not at all — three entrypoints here were written this way and two of them shipped unable to run
workaround: wrap the awaiting tail in an async main() and call it; nothing else changes, and the failure is a bundle-time error rather than a runtime one so tests that only run under tsx will not catch it

evidence.output:
✘ [ERROR] Top-level await is currently not supported with the "cjs" output format
      183 │ await server.connect(new StdioServerTransport());

check.confirmedIf: esbuild exits non-zero on a cjs bundle containing top-level await

observations.note: Hit three times in one day in this repository: record.ts, gate.ts and the MCP server were all written with a top-level await and all failed at bundle time rather than at runtime, so each ran correctly under tsx and shipped unable to run.
